text: main entry point read_lasa_sav(), detects LASA datafile ’re working dispatches correct import/cleaning function automatically: LASA046 files specifically, apply_lasa046_labels() applies SPSS variable- value-labels imports data correctly. current version supports waves: B, C, D, E, 2B, F, G, H, MB, 3B, , J, K future, similar functions built datafiles. importing, can check whether variables matched LASA documentation using lasa_label_report(): returns set “faulty” variables — ones couldn’t matched corresponding documentation — can inspect resolve analysis.
code: library(CleanLASA)  # Import and label a LASA .sav file  # importing the data should generally be in this fomrat: data <- read_lasa_sav("path/to/LASA[wave][file_code].sav")  # Specific examples: data <- read_lasa_sav("LASAB046.sav") # LASA wave B file 046 data <- read_lasa_sav("LASA_data/LASAZ004.sav") # LASA wave Z file 004 data <- read_lasa_sav("Documents/Research/data/LAS2B011.sav") # LASA wave 2B file 011 data <- read_lasa_sav("lasazoa1.sav") # LASA wave Z file oa1 data <- read_lasa_sav("LASAJFI.sav") # LASA wave J file FI # Specifically for LASA046 (Physical Activity), datapath should be in this format: data <- apply_lasa046_labels("path/to/LASA[wave]046.sav")  # Examples data <- apply_lasa046_labels("LASAC046.sav") data <- apply_lasa046_labels("LASMB046.sav") data <- apply_lasa046_labels("LAS3B046.sav") lasa_label_report(data)

title: Apply LASA 046 variable labels, value labels, and optional harmonisation — apply_lasa046_labels
text: data data frame tibble containing one LASA 046 data file. wave Character scalar identifying LASA measurement wave. Supported values "B", "C", "D", "E", "2B", "F", "G", "H", "3B", "MB", "", "J", "K". Matching case-insensitive. wave must supplied explicitly B, 2B, 3B, MB use b variable-name prefix labels coding rules differ. fuzzy_match Logical scalar. TRUE (default), permit conservative fuzzy matching likely variable-name typing errors exact, case-insensitive, punctuation-insensitive matching failed. max_edit_distance Non-negative integer giving maximum edit distance accepted automatic fuzzy matching. Defaults 1. name_corrections Optional named character vector explicit variable-name corrections. Vector names canonical LASA suffixes ("respnr") values corresponding column names data, example c(lphya08 = "BLPYA08", respnr = "RespNrr"). Explicit corrections take precedence automatic matching. warn_unmatched Logical scalar. TRUE (default), issue warning expected variable matched confidently, match ambiguous, manual correction fails, respondent identifier inferred first-column position. Successful fuzzy matches reported message audit trigger warning. to_factor Logical scalar. FALSE (default), variables substantive value labels remain numeric/haven-labelled receive SPSS-style "labels" attributes. TRUE, variables converted factors using LASA value labels factor-level labels. observed value without codebook value label retained factor level rather converted NA. to_numeric Logical scalar. FALSE (default), count, duration, numeric variables retain documented negative missing-reason value labels. TRUE, variable treated substantive numeric every value label documented negative missing-reason code. variables converted ordinary numeric vectors, every observed value zero replaced NA, non-negative values retained. variables to_numeric = TRUE takes precedence to_factor = TRUE. standardize_names Logical scalar. FALSE (default), original source column names retained. TRUE, every successfully matched LASA 046 variable renamed canonical lowercase LASA documentation name supplied wave (example blphya01, clphya26, klphya50) first-column respondent identifier renamed respnr. Unmatched non-046 columns left unchanged.

title: Apply LASA 046 variable labels, value labels, and optional harmonisation — apply_lasa046_labels
text: Variable-name matching. Matching proceeds following order: explicit name_corrections; exact name; case-insensitive exact name; normalized exact name, ignoring punctuation/underscores; optionally, unique fuzzy match within max_edit_distance. Fuzzy matching deliberately conservative. Correctly formed LASA 046 names belonging another questionnaire item protected selected merely edit distance small. Respondent number. first column expected contain respondent number. Capitalization minor spelling variants respnr handled matching logic. first-column position structural invariant files, first column used final fallback name matched; flagged audit. Numeric versus categorical conversion. to_numeric simply convert every labelled variable numeric. variable identified substantive numeric variable codebook value labels negative missing-reason codes. distinguishes variables numbers occasions minutes categorical variables whose substantive codes labels "", "yes", sport categories. to_factor = TRUE to_numeric = TRUE, numeric/count/duration variables become ordinary numeric vectors negative codes set NA, categorical variables become factors. Name harmonisation. Canonical renaming performed matching complete, changing earlier column name alter later matching decisions. function stops rather creating duplicate names canonical name collide another column. Audit provenance. returned object contains generic matching audit attr(x, "label_report"). also receives "LASA_wave", "LASA_file_code", "LASA_names_standardized" attributes. generic names shared future LASA label implementations can inspected lasa_label_report().

text: filecode single non-empty character string containing LASA data-file code, "046", "z004", "zoa2". optional "LASA" prefix accepted. viewer open codebook. One : "auto" Use RStudio Viewer available otherwise use system's default browser PDF viewer. "rstudio" Attempt use RStudio Viewer fall back system's default browser PDF viewer unavailable. title: Open a LASA variable-information codebook — lasa_var_info
text: Codebooks downloaded directly public LASA website, exported wit package inst/codebooks/ directory. RStudio, function first attempts display PDF Viewer pane. RStudio Viewer unavailable open file, PDF opened system's default browser PDF viewer. Codebook filenames derived automatically filecode according LASA naming conventions: Standard data files: LASA[filecode]_varinfo.pdf, example LASA046_varinfo.pdf. Z-files: LASAz[number]_varinfo.pdf, example LASAz004_varinfo.pdf. Algorithm-based osteoarthritis files zoa1, zoa2, zoa3: LASAzoa1_2_3_varinfo.pdf. Filename matching case-insensitive. Consequently, file codes may supplied without LASA prefix upper- lowercase.

text: dispatcher follows LASA filename convention: regular single-letter waves: LASA[wave][file_code].SAV, e.g. LASAE046.SAV; waves 2B, 3B, 4B, MB: LAS[wave][file_code].SAV, e.g. LAS3B046.SAV; information stored across waves: wave code Z, e.g. LASAZ004.SAV; file codes contain 2 3 alphanumeric characters interpreted case-insensitively. File-specific label functions selected convention. file code starts number, expected function apply_lasa[file_code]_labels(); example, file 046 maps apply_lasa046_labels() file 004 maps apply_lasa004_labels(). file code starts letter, expected function apply_lasa_[file_code]_labels(); example, FI maps apply_lasa_fi_labels(). OA files oa1, oa2, oa3 hard-coded family map apply_lasa_oa_labels(). selected function must already available package namespace current R session. wrapper always supplies data. supplies wave argument exists selected function's formal arguments (checked via formals()), supplies file_code argument exists. permits shared implementations future apply_lasa_oa_labels(data, file_code, ...) retaining standard wave-aware interface used apply_lasa046_labels(data, wave, ...). Arguments supplied ... reserved selected label function, haven::read_sav(). validated function's formal arguments passed .call(). example, file 046 detected, to_factor = TRUE, to_numeric = TRUE, standardize_names = TRUE, name_corrections = ... passed directly apply_lasa046_labels(). Additional SPSS import options belong read_sav_args. labelling, generic provenance attributes attached: "LASA_wave", "LASA_file_code", "LASA_source_file", "LASA_label_function". File-specific functions attach variable-name audit generic "label_report" attribute.

title: Read and label a LASA SPSS data file — read_lasa_sav
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Automatically dispatches to apply_lasa046_labels() dat_e <- read_lasa_sav(   "LASAE046.SAV",   to_factor = TRUE,   to_numeric = TRUE,   standardize_names = TRUE,   name_corrections = c(lphya08 = "ELPYA08") )  # Also dispatches to apply_lasa046_labels(), with wave = "3B" dat_3b <- read_lasa_sav("LAS3B046.SAV")  # Dispatches to apply_lasa004_labels() once that function exists dat_z004 <- read_lasa_sav("LASAZ004.SAV")  # Both dispatch to apply_lasa_oa_labels() once that function exists oa1 <- read_lasa_sav("LASAzoa1.sav") oa2 <- read_lasa_sav("LASAzoa2.sav") } # }
